content.value_statement: Reusable cloud infrastructure is hard to standardize across teams. This skill guides AWS CDK patterns, L2 constructs, IAM, monitoring, tagging, and stack boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Guides reusable AWS CDK construct and stack design.
Recommends L2 constructs over L1 constructs when practical.
Explains separation of stateful and stateless infrastructure stacks.
Provides a serverless API pattern using API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB.
Emphasizes least privilege IAM, tagging, monitoring, tracing, and removal policies.
Supports CDK review for common best practices and anti-patterns.
limitations: It does not cover Terraform-specific workflows.
It does not focus on raw CloudFormation template authoring.
Examples must be adapted, synthesized, and reviewed before deployment.
It does not replace organization-specific security and compliance checks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Create repeatable CDK patterns for APIs, compute, storage, and shared resources.

use_cases.title: Review CDK Stack Quality
use_cases.description: Check construct choices, IAM scope, stack boundaries, tagging, monitoring, and deployment readiness.

use_cases.title: Design Production Serverless Apps
use_cases.description: Plan API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, tracing, alarms, and retention settings as one reusable pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a CDK Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to build an AWS service with CDK. Ask me the key questions, then recommend a reusable pattern and stack structure.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Serverless API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reusable CDK serverless API pattern with API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, tracing, alarms, tags, and least privilege IAM.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this CDK stack for L1 construct use, IAM scope, removal policies, tags, monitoring, and stateful versus stateless separation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Multi-Stack Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose a multi-stack CDK architecture for a production application with shared stateful resources, stateless services, observability, and deployment guardrails.

output_examples.input: Design a reusable serverless API pattern for AWS CDK.
output: The skill would recommend separate data and service stacks.
It would include API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB, tracing, alarms, tagging, and least privilege permissions.
It would call out deployment checks such as synthesizing and reviewing the infrastructure diff.

output_examples.input: Review my CDK construct for production readiness.
output: The skill would flag overly broad IAM permissions, missing tags, missing monitoring, and weak removal policies.
It would suggest L2 constructs where they provide safer defaults.
It would recommend clearer boundaries between persistent resources and deployable service resources.

output_examples.input: Plan shared CDK patterns for a platform team.
output: The skill would identify reusable constructs for common service types.
It would suggest consistent tagging, observability, and account or region configuration practices.
It would describe how teams can adapt the patterns without duplicating infrastructure logic.

best_practices: Prefer L2 constructs because they usually provide clearer interfaces and safer defaults.
Separate persistent resources from stateless service resources to reduce deployment risk.
Review generated infrastructure changes before deployment and apply least privilege permissions.
anti_patterns: Using low-level constructs when maintained L2 constructs meet the requirement.
Combining databases, queues, compute, and APIs into one tightly coupled stack.
Hardcoding accounts, regions, names, or broad IAM permissions in reusable constructs.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design reusable AWS CDK patterns, stacks, and constructs for common cloud infrastructure needs.

faq.question: Which CDK languages does it mention?
faq.answer: The skill description mentions TypeScript, Python, and Java.

faq.question: Does it support Terraform?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that Terraform-specific tasks are outside its scope.

faq.question: Can it review existing CDK code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide reviews for CDK best practices, anti-patterns, IAM scope, monitoring, and stack structure.

faq.question: Does it deploy infrastructure automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides design and review guidance. Users should run their normal synthesis, diff, testing, and deployment workflow.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: It includes production-oriented guidance such as least privilege IAM, monitoring, tracing, tags, and removal policies.
